The engine owns subscription state. A gateway charges and refunds; what a subscription IS, when it renews and what it costs is decided here, so nothing changes underneath you when a provider does.

**Every money-moving operation has an estimate that does not move money.** `estimate`, `cancel_estimate`, `reactivate_estimate`, `renewal_estimate` and `subscription_estimate` return the exact proration, tax and credit the real call would produce. Show one to a customer before you charge them.

Two ways to change items, and picking the wrong one is the usual mistake. `change` applies a **delta** — these items added, those removed. `update_for_items` reconciles against a **desired final set** and removes anything absent from it. A delta sent to the second endpoint deletes everything you did not mention.

Anything dated can be scheduled instead of applied: cancel, pause, resume and change all take a future date, and a pending schedule can be listed and withdrawn before it fires.
